question: A 29-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 0 at 11 weeks' gestation comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of left lower extremity pain and swelling. Her temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F). Physical examination shows a tender, palpable cord on the lateral aspect of the left lower leg. The overlying skin is erythematous and indurated. Duplex ultrasound shows vascular wall thickening and subcutaneous edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The patient's symptoms of left lower extremity pain, swelling, and the presence of a tender, palpable cord along with erythema and induration suggest inflammation of a superficial vein. The duplex ultrasound findings of vascular wall thickening and subcutaneous edema further support this diagnosis. These findings are consistent with superficial thrombophlebitis, which is inflammation of a superficial vein often associated with thrombosis. Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) typically presents with more significant swelling and may not have a palpable cord. Erysipelas and erythema nodosum have different clinical presentations and are less likely given the ultrasound findings. Varicose veins do not typically present with acute pain and inflammation as described.
